title: EC, Dissolved Ions and Root-Zone Trend Analysis

content.overview: Electrical conductivity provides a practical estimate of total dissolved ionic concentration. It is useful for comparing source water, nutrient solution, drainage, and root-zone extracts, but it does not reveal which specific ions are present.

vocabulary.definition: A measure of how readily a solution conducts electrical current, influenced by the concentration and mobility of dissolved ions.
Electrical conductivity measured from the solution associated with the root environment using a defined sampling method.
A directional pattern in repeated measurements over time rather than one isolated value.

sections.title: EC measures total ionic concentration
sections.body: Different mixtures of ions can produce similar EC values. EC therefore helps track overall concentration but cannot substitute for nutrient-specific chemical analysis.

sections.title: Sampling method changes the number
sections.body: Feed solution, runoff, pore-water extracts, and saturated-media extracts are not directly interchangeable. Comparisons should use a consistent method and record where and when the sample was taken.

sections.title: Trends reveal accumulation or dilution
sections.body: Repeated EC data can help identify whether the root zone is concentrating salts, being diluted, or remaining relatively stable. Interpretation should include irrigation volume, dryback, plant demand, and source-water EC.

workedExamples: If feed EC remains steady while root-zone EC rises over several irrigations, investigate water removal, dryback, drainage, and plant uptake before simply increasing feed concentration.
If source-water EC changes seasonally, record the new baseline so nutrient-solution comparisons remain meaningful.
commonMistakes: Assuming EC identifies individual nutrient concentrations.
Comparing runoff EC directly with a different extraction method.
Reacting to one measurement without checking the trend.
content.practicalApplication: Measure source, feed, and root-zone EC using documented methods, record the timing relative to irrigation, graph repeated values, and interpret the trend with moisture and plant observations.
content.summary: EC is a concentration and trend tool, not a nutrient-specific assay. Consistent sampling and repeated measurements make it useful for diagnosing root-zone accumulation and irrigation behavior.
